criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a named end-to-end test feeds a result event through the stream parser and the claude driver (fake script) or the invocation constructor. Its top-level usage differs from modelUsage (main thread plus subagent usage on the requested model, using 90/52656/3634696/134508 against 6/3136/275219/3821). It then runs check_invocation on the resulting record and asserts there is no Reconciliation violation.
criteria.evidence: invocation::tests::a_result_with_subagent_usage_reconciles_end_to_end passed when I ran it. It passes JOB_2FSA_RESULT (top-level 6/3136/275219/3821, modelUsage on the requested model claude-sonnet-5-5 at 90/52656/3634696/134508) through StreamState::on_line, then output_from_result (the builder the Claude driver now calls), then Athena::invocation_record. It asserts the record holds 90/52656/3634696/134508 and that check_invocation finds no Reconciliation violation. On the base, the parser kept the top-level usage, so the record would hold 6/3136/... and fail the old requested-model comparison. The test would therefore fail without the fix.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a named negative test builds the record from a result event whose totals really disagree with modelUsage, through the same path. It asserts that check_invocation returns a Reconciliation violation.
criteria.evidence: a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end passes, but neither of its two cases is what the criterion asks for. (a) RESULT_WITHOUT_MODEL_USAGE does go through the path, but the event has no modelUsage at all. The violation it gets comes from the `None =>` branch of check_invocation ('measured tokens, but no usage for the requested model', reconcile.rs:111). So nothing disagrees with modelUsage, and the new sum-versus-recorded comparison is never reached. (b) The 2fsa case sets record.tokens.output by hand after invocation_record returns. That skips the path, which is exactly the artificial setup that 'really disagree … through the same path' rules out. Since the parser now derives usage from modelUsage, token totals cannot disagree through the path. A real disagreement could still be built: for example, an event whose total_cost_usd differs from the modelUsage costUSD sum, which also produces a Reconciliation violation. The producer could also have said the token case cannot happen. It did neither.

criteria.criterion: One definition of an invocation's measured tokens is stated in a doc comment (on ResultEvent.usage and AgentOutput.usage in lib.rs). The invocation record and the gate's reconcile rule both use it.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: doc comments were added on ResultEvent::usage (stream.rs) and AgentOutput::usage (lib.rs), both saying the definition is the sum of modelUsage over every model, with top-level usage used only when modelUsage is absent. parse_result sets usage to that sum. output_from_result copies result.usage, and invocation_record records output.usage with its basis now set to 'result.modelUsage, summed over models'. check_invocation compares the recorded tokens with the sum over models_used. It also accepts the legacy requested-model-only shape, which the reading allowed.

criteria.criterion: The job 2fsa numbers (90/52656/3634696/134508 and 6/3136/275219/3821) appear in a regression test fixture or comment, and CHANGELOG.md records the fix.
criteria.evidence: The numbers appear in fixtures in stream.rs (RESULT_WITH_SUBAGENTS), invocation.rs (JOB_2FSA_RESULT) and the claude.rs fake script's 'subagents' mode, each with a comment. CHANGELOG.md under Changed records the fix and names the root cause.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check: all pass and are clean, including the existing stream, claude and landing tests.
criteria.evidence: fmt and clippy produced no output and exited 0. Every test binary in cargo test reported ok with 0 failed; the ignored tests were already ignored.

findings.summary: The negative end-to-end test never builds a record from an event whose totals really disagree with modelUsage, through the same path.
findings.evidence: Case 1 uses an event with no modelUsage, which hits the 'no usage for the requested model' branch rather than the new sum comparison. Case 2 changes record.tokens.output by hand after the record is built, which skips the path. Suggested fixes: add a through-path event that really disagrees, such as total_cost_usd not equal to the modelUsage costUSD sum. Or state, in the test and the changelog, that token disagreement cannot happen through the parser under the new definition, and keep the hand-changed case labelled as a gate-only check.

findings.summary: The legacy exception means a new multi-model record holding only the requested model's tokens also passes.
findings.evidence: reconcile.rs:105 `recorded != (si, so, sr, sw) && recorded != legacy`. The reading allowed this to keep older records/ passing, but it applies to every record, not only older ones. records/ is not in the snapshot, so I could not check how many older records need it.

findings.summary: Two expected deliverables were left unchanged.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs and crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs are on the list but not in the diff. No file outside the list was changed.

summary: The change fixes the root cause: the stream parser now sets an invocation's tokens to the sum of modelUsage. That definition is written on ResultEvent::usage and AgentOutput::usage, and the gate compares the record against the same sum. The positive end-to-end test (a_result_with_subagent_usage_reconciles_end_to_end) runs job 2fsa's result event through the parser, the driver's output builder, the invocation constructor and check_invocation, and would fail without the fix. fmt, clippy and the full test suite all pass when I ran them. Criterion 2 is not met. The negative test's only case that goes through the path uses an event with no modelUsage, which hits the 'no usage for the requested model' branch, so nothing actually disagrees. Its other case changes the record by hand after it is built, which skips the path. The fix is either a through-path event that really disagrees (for example, a cost total that differs from the modelUsage costs) or a stated reason why token disagreement cannot happen under the new definition.
